limitations: Decoding is entirely `org.modkitx/zip`'s. This codec owns the `.wz` extension and the Warzone-specific package classification; it does not implement a ZIP reader. `.wz` was removed from the common zip codec's `match` in the same change, because a shared codec must not carry one game's extension.

Node only, because the delegated `org.modkitx/zip` is. Statically importing it reaches `fs/promises` and `buffer` in the ZIP reader, `worker_threads` through fflate's node build, and `fs`/`crypto` through the 7z bridge used for encrypted entries. Declaring browser environments here would be a claim the import graph contradicts, and the catalog validator checks exactly that.

Classification prefers the package's own root `ruleset.json` over any filename rule, and the path over a bare filename. A renamed `base.wz` is still a campaign ruleset, and a mod named `mp.wz` under `mods/` is still a mod.
The caller supplies `ruleset.json`; this codec does not read it out of the archive itself, so classification degrades to path and filename when it is not provided.
Read only. Writing a `.wz` back is not implemented, though the delegated ZIP codec is capable of it.
`.scd` (Supreme Commander) remains on the common zip codec and is the same shape of misplaced knowledge. Moving it needs a Supreme Commander extension, which does not exist.
